topic: What happens if you swallow chewing gum?
title: What Happens If You Swallow Chewing Gum?
sources: Mayo Clinic, 'Is it true that swallowed gum stays in your stomach for 7 years?' (mayoclinic.org, healthy-adult facts): gum base is indigestible, but a swallowed piece is moved through the digestive tract by normal gut motion and is excreted in stool, usually within a few days; the 7-years myth is false

Milov DE, Andres JM, Erhart NA, Bailey DJ. 'Chewing gum bezoars of the gastrointestinal tract.' Pediatrics 1998;102(2):e22 (PMID 9685468): children who swallowed gum daily (several pieces, in one case with coins) developed gum bezoars — hardened masses that caused blockages; one 4-year-old required surgical removal

Sinopidis X, Zachos K, Panagidis A, et al. 'Chewing gum bezoar as an unexpected cause of acute intestinal obstruction.' J Paediatr Child Health 2021;57(9):1533-1535 (PMID 33373485): gum bezoar causing acute intestinal obstruction in a child

lines.text: What happens if you swallow your chewing gum?
Gum base is a synthetic rubber your stomach ignores.
Your gut muscles just push it through.
One piece usually leaves within a few days.
The seven years myth is just that, a myth.
lines.caps: The *7 years | myth is | just a *myth

lines.text: But swallow gum every day, and it can pile up.
lines.caps: But *swallow it | *every day | and it *piles up

lines.text: Doctors have pulled out hard gum masses from kids.
Some even needed surgery for the blockage.
So gum is for chewing, not swallowing.
Your gut forgives once, not a habit.
